13	**WHEREAS**, the Participant is currently employed by the Company as its Chief Revenue Officer pursuant to that certain Executive Employment Agreement dated July 22, 2021, by and between the Company and the Participant (the \"Employment Agreement\"); and
14	
15	**WHEREAS**, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors (the \"Committee\") has determined that it is in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders to grant to the Participant the Restricted Stock Units described herein, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement and the Plan.
16	
17	**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Company and the Participant agree as follows:
18	
19	Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Plan.
20	
21	**[ARTICLE I --- GRANT OF RESTRICTED STOCK UNITS]{.underline}**
22	
23	**Section 1.1 --- Grant.** The Company hereby grants to the Participant twenty-eight thousand (28,000) Restricted Stock Units (the \"RSUs\"), effective as of the Grant Date. Each RSU represents the right to receive one (1) share of the Company\'s common stock, par value \$0.001 per share (\"Common Stock\"), subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Plan. The RSUs are granted under and pursuant to the Plan and are subject in all respects to the terms and provisions of the Plan, which are incorporated herein by reference.
24	
25	**Section 1.2 --- Nature of RSUs.** The RSUs granted hereunder are unfunded, unsecured bookkeeping entries maintained by the Company on its records. No shares of Common Stock shall be issued to the Participant at the time of grant. The RSUs shall not entitle the Participant to any rights of a stockholder of the Company, including without limitation the right to vote shares of Common Stock, to receive dividends or dividend equivalents, or to exercise any other rights appurtenant to ownership of Common Stock, unless and until shares of Common Stock are actually delivered to the Participant upon vesting and settlement of the RSUs in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. The RSUs are non-transferable and may not be sold, pledged, assigned, hypothecated, encumbered, or otherwise transferred or disposed of by the Participant, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, except by will or the laws of descent and distribution.
26	
27	**Section 1.3 --- Consideration.** The RSUs are granted in consideration of the Participant\'s continued employment with the Company and its Affiliates, the past, present, and future services to be rendered by the Participant to the Company and its Affiliates, and the Participant\'s agreement to be bound by the restrictive covenants and other obligations set forth in this Agreement, including without limitation the covenants contained in Article VI hereof.
28	
29	**[ARTICLE II --- VESTING]{.underline}**
30	
31	**Section 2.1 --- Vesting Schedule.** Subject to the Participant\'s continued employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates through each applicable Vesting Date (as defined below) and to the other terms and conditions of this Agreement, the RSUs shall vest in four (4) equal annual installments of seven thousand (7,000) RSUs each, on the dates set forth below (each, a \"Vesting Date\"):
32	
33	> \(a\) **First Installment:** Seven thousand (7,000) RSUs shall vest on March 1, 2023;
34	>
35	> \(b\) **Second Installment:** Seven thousand (7,000) RSUs shall vest on March 1, 2024;
36	>
37	> \(c\) **Third Installment:** Seven thousand (7,000) RSUs shall vest on March 1, 2025; and
38	>
39	> \(d\) **Fourth Installment:** Seven thousand (7,000) RSUs shall vest on March 1, 2026.
40	
41	The vesting schedule set forth above is summarized in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.
42	
43	**Section 2.2 --- Termination of Employment --- Effect on Vesting.** The effect of the termination of the Participant\'s employment on the vesting of RSUs shall be as follows:
44	
45	> \(a\) *Termination for Cause.* If the Participant\'s employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates is terminated by the Company for \"Cause\" (as defined in the Employment Agreement, as may be amended from time to time), all RSUs that have not vested as of the date of such termination shall be immediately and automatically forfeited by the Participant without any consideration or further action required on the part of the Company. Such forfeiture shall be effective as of the date of termination of employment.
46	>
47	> \(b\) *Termination Without Cause.* If the Participant\'s employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates is terminated by the Company without Cause (and not due to death or Disability), all RSUs that have not vested as of the date of such termination shall be forfeited by the Participant as of the date of termination without any consideration; provided, however, that such forfeiture shall be without prejudice to the clawback and repayment provisions set forth in Article VII of this Agreement, which shall remain in full force and effect following such termination.
48	>
49	> \(c\) *Voluntary Resignation.* If the Participant voluntarily resigns from employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates (including a resignation for Good Reason, if applicable, except as otherwise provided in Section 2.3), all RSUs that have not vested as of the date of such resignation shall be immediately and automatically forfeited by the Participant without any consideration.
50	>
51	> \(d\) *Death or Disability.* In the event of the Participant\'s death or Disability (as defined in the Plan) while the Participant is employed by the Company or any of its Affiliates, any RSUs that have not yet vested but that would have vested within the twelve (12)-month period immediately following the date of the Participant\'s death or Disability shall become vested as of such date. All RSUs that would not have vested within such twelve (12)-month period shall be immediately and automatically forfeited without any consideration.
52	>
53	> \(e\) *No Partial Vesting.* For the avoidance of doubt, there shall be no pro-rata or partial vesting of any individual tranche of RSUs. Each tranche as set forth in Section 2.1 shall vest in full on the applicable Vesting Date or shall not vest at all, except as expressly provided in Section 2.2(d) or Section 2.3.
54	
55	**Section 2.3 --- Change in Control.** In the event of a Change in Control (as defined in the Plan), the Committee may, in its sole and absolute discretion, accelerate vesting of all or any portion of the unvested RSUs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Participant\'s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause or, to the extent applicable under the Employment Agreement, the Participant resigns for Good Reason, in either case within twelve (12) months following the effective date of a Change in Control, all RSUs that have not yet vested as of the date of such termination or resignation shall become fully vested as of such date.
56	
57	**[ARTICLE III --- SETTLEMENT AND DELIVERY OF SHARES]{.underline}**
58	
59	**Section 3.1 --- Settlement.** Within thirty (30) days following each Vesting Date (or, in the case of accelerated vesting pursuant to Section 2.2(d) or Section 2.3, within thirty (30) days following the date on which such accelerated vesting occurs), the Company shall deliver to the Participant one (1) share of Common Stock for each RSU that has become vested, net of any shares withheld pursuant to Section 3.2 hereof. Upon delivery of shares, the corresponding RSUs shall be cancelled and the Participant shall have no further rights with respect to such RSUs.
60	
61	**Section 3.2 --- Tax Withholding.** The Company shall have the right and obligation to withhold from shares of Common Stock otherwise deliverable to the Participant upon the vesting and settlement of RSUs, or to require the Participant to remit to the Company, an amount sufficient to satisfy all applicable federal, state, and local income tax and employment tax withholding obligations arising in connection with the vesting and settlement of the RSUs. The Company may, in its sole discretion, satisfy such withholding obligations by any one or a combination of the following methods: (a) withholding shares of Common Stock from the shares otherwise deliverable to the Participant, which withheld shares shall have a Fair Market Value (as defined in Section 4.1) on the date of vesting equal to the minimum statutory withholding amount (or such greater amount as may be permitted without resulting in adverse accounting consequences); (b) deducting the applicable withholding amount from any cash compensation or other amounts payable to the Participant by the Company; or (c) requiring the Participant to make a cash payment to the Company in the amount of the required withholding.
62	
63	**Section 3.3 --- Section 409A Compliance.** This Agreement is intended to comply with, or to be exempt from, the requirements of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (\"Section 409A\"), and the regulations and guidance promulgated thereunder, and shall be interpreted and construed consistently with such intent. The settlement and delivery of shares of Common Stock in respect of vested RSUs shall be made in a manner and at such times as comply with the requirements of Section 409A to the extent applicable. If the Participant is a \"specified employee\" within the meaning of Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) of the Internal Revenue Code at the time of the Participant\'s \"separation from service\" within the meaning of Section 409A, then to the extent any settlement of RSUs constitutes \"deferred compensation\" subject to Section 409A, such settlement shall be delayed until the date that is six (6) months and one (1) day following the date of such separation from service, or, if earlier, the date of the Participant\'s death, to the extent required to avoid the imposition of additional taxes and penalties under Section 409A.

71	> \(b\) **\"Cause\"** shall have the meaning ascribed to such term in the Employment Agreement between the Company and the Participant, dated July 22, 2021, as may be amended from time to time.

77	> \(e\) **\"Employment Agreement\"** means the Executive Employment Agreement between the Company and the Participant dated July 22, 2021, as may be amended from time to time.

81	> \(g\) **\"Grant Date\"** means March 1, 2022.

83	> \(h\) **\"Plan\"** means the Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. 2019 Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan, as amended from time to time.
84	>
85	> \(i\) **\"Restricted Period\"** means the twelve (12)-month period commencing on the date of the Participant\'s termination of employment with the Company for any reason.
86	>
87	> \(j\) **\"RSU\"** or **\"Restricted Stock Unit\"** means a bookkeeping entry representing the contingent right to receive one (1) share of Common Stock, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Plan.

93	> \(a\) The Participant has received, read, and understands this Agreement and the Plan, and has had the opportunity to review both documents carefully before executing this Agreement.

95	> \(b\) The grant of RSUs pursuant to this Agreement is a one-time, discretionary award and does not create any contractual or other right to receive future grants of restricted stock units, stock options, or any other awards under the Plan or otherwise. The grant of RSUs does not guarantee the Participant\'s continued employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates for any period of time.
96	>
97	> \(c\) The value of the RSUs and the underlying shares of Common Stock is subject to fluctuation and may increase or decrease over time. The Company makes no representation or guarantee regarding the future value of the Common Stock. The Participant acknowledges that the RSUs may have no value at the time of vesting.
98	>
99	> \(d\) The RSUs and the shares of Common Stock issuable upon settlement thereof constitute an extraordinary item of compensation that is outside the scope of the Participant\'s regular employment compensation. The RSUs shall not be considered part of the Participant\'s normal or expected compensation for purposes of calculating any severance, resignation, redundancy, termination, end-of-service payment, bonus, pension, retirement, or similar benefit or payment under any plan, program, policy, or arrangement of the Company or any of its Affiliates.
100	>
101	> \(e\) The Participant has had the opportunity to consult with independent legal and tax counsel regarding this Agreement, the RSUs, and the tax consequences associated therewith, and the Participant is not relying on the Company or any of its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, or agents for any legal or tax advice in connection with this Agreement.

103	**Section 5.2 --- No Right to Continued Employment.** Nothing in this Agreement shall confer upon the Participant any right to continue in the employ of the Company or any Affiliate, or shall interfere with or restrict in any way the right of the Company or any Affiliate to terminate the Participant\'s employment at any time for any reason, with or without Cause, subject to the terms of the Employment Agreement.

105	**[ARTICLE VI --- RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS]{.underline}**
106	
107	**Section 6.1 --- Acknowledgment of Protectable Interests.** The Participant acknowledges and agrees that: (a) in the course of the Participant\'s employment with the Company, the Participant has had and will continue to have access to Confidential Information, trade secrets, proprietary business methods, customer and supplier relationships, strategic plans, pricing information, product development pipelines, and the goodwill of the Company and its Affiliates; (b) the grant of RSUs pursuant to this Agreement provides the Participant with valuable consideration sufficient to support the restrictive covenants set forth in this Article VI; and (c) the restrictions set forth in this Article VI are reasonable in scope, duration, and geographic extent and are necessary to protect the Company\'s legitimate business interests, including its Confidential Information, trade secrets, customer relationships, and goodwill.
108	
109	**Section 6.2 --- Non-Competition.** During the term of the Participant\'s employment with the Company and during the Restricted Period, the Participant shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as an employee, officer, director, consultant, advisor, independent contractor, agent, partner, member, stockholder (other than as a passive holder of less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding equity securities of a publicly traded company), joint venturer, or in any other capacity, anywhere in the United States and Canada:

118	
119	**Section 6.4 --- Remedies.** The Participant acknowledges and agrees that a breach or threatened breach of any of the covenants contained in this Article VI would cause irreparable harm to the Company for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, in the event of any such breach or threatened breach, the Company shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief (including temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, and permanent injunctions) to enforce the covenants contained herein, in addition to any other remedies available to the Company at law or in equity, including without limitation monetary damages. In addition, the provisions of Article VII (Clawback and Forfeiture) of this Agreement shall apply in the event of a breach of this Article VI, and such provisions are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the Company\'s other remedies.
120	
121	**[ARTICLE VII --- CLAWBACK AND FORFEITURE]{.underline}**
122	
123	**Section 7.1 --- Forfeiture of Unvested RSUs.** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement to the contrary, if at any time during the term of this Agreement: (a) the Participant\'s employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates is terminated by the Company for Cause, or (b) the Participant breaches any provision of Article VI of this Agreement, then all RSUs that have not vested as of the date of such termination or, in the case of a breach of Article VI, as of the date on which the Company determines that such breach has occurred, shall be immediately and automatically forfeited by the Participant without any consideration. 124	
125	**Section 7.2 --- Clawback of Vested RSUs.** If the Participant\'s employment with the Company or any of its Affiliates is terminated by the Company for Cause, or if the Participant breaches any restrictive covenant set forth in Article VI of this Agreement (whether during or following the Participant\'s employment), the Participant shall, within thirty (30) days following written demand by the Company, repay to the Company in cash an amount equal to the aggregate pre-tax Fair Market Value of any RSUs that vested during the eighteen (18)-month period immediately preceding the date of such termination of employment or the date on which the breach is determined by the Company to have occurred, whichever is applicable (such eighteen (18)-month period, the \"Clawback Period\"). 126	
127	**Section 7.3 --- No Limitation on Other Remedies.** The forfeiture and clawback provisions set forth in this Article VII are in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other remedies available to the Company, including without limitation the right to seek injunctive relief, monetary damages (including consequential and incidental damages), specific performance, and any remedies available under the Employment Agreement, the Plan, or applicable law. 128	
129	**Section 7.4 --- Compliance with Applicable Law.** The clawback and forfeiture provisions of this Article VII are in addition to, and not in limitation of, any clawback, recoupment, or forfeiture provisions required by applicable law, including without limitation Section 10D of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and any rules or regulations promulgated thereunder by the Securities and Exchange Commission or any national securities exchange on which the Common Stock is listed, and any clawback, recoupment, or forfeiture policy adopted by the Company or the Board of Directors of the Company from time to time in compliance with such requirements. To the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or Company policy, additional clawback, recoupment, or forfeiture provisions may apply to the RSUs granted hereunder, and the Participant agrees to comply with any such requirements.

131	**[ARTICLE VIII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

133	**Section 8.1 --- Plan Controls.** This Agreement is subject to and governed by the terms and provisions of the Plan, which are incorporated herein by reference. B("**Consideration for the Amendment is weak and, in our view, likely inadequate under North Carolina law for the broadened covenants.** The only stated consideration is “continued employment” and “the designation of Executive as Chief Revenue Officer” — a title Manheim already held under Section 2.1 of the Original Agreement since August 2021. North Carolina requires new, independent consideration to support a non-compete entered into or expanded after employment begins; continued at-will employment is not enough. B("**The RSU non-compete differs materially from the employment non-compete and only it triggers the equity clawback.** RSU Section 6.2 runs 12 months (vs. 18 original / 24 amended), covers any “Competitive Business” that “competes with the Company in the household cleaning products industry” (no revenue threshold; no personal care or home fragrance), is governed by Delaware law, and has no forum clause. After September 1, 2025, the RSU clawback leverage is **zero** even though the RSU non-compete runs to February 2026.")
B("**Garden leave does not offset severance in a Company-initiated termination.** Amendment Section 7 (new “Section 7(e)”) applies only during a 90-day Notice Period that begins with **Manheim’s** notice of voluntary resignation. The dollar-for-dollar credit in clause (iv) applies only if the Company elected garden leave during that Notice Period and then terminated without Cause. If Pinnacle initiates a without-Cause termination in February 2025, there is no Notice Period, no garden leave election is available, and **no offset applies**: gross and net severance are the same. Even where the credit does apply, it does not reduce Pinnacle’s total cash cost — it prevents double payment ($117,123 paid as garden leave salary instead of as severance).")
B("**Severance exposure (without Cause, termination February 28, 2025, fiscal year = calendar year assumed):** base salary continuation **$475,000** + pro-rated FY2025 bonus (**$53,747** at target; range $0–$80,620 at 0–150%) + COBRA reimbursement up to **$25,200** = approximately **$553,947** at target (plus Accrued Obligations). All of it is conditioned on a timely Release and continuing covenant compliance and is subject to cessation and repayment upon breach (EA Section 6.2; Amendment Section 9). Manheim would also likely forfeit any unpaid FY2024 bonus if terminated before the FY2024 bonus payment date (EA Section 3.2) — a point he will contest.")
B("**Non-disparagement / McLaren Macomb.** As CRO, Manheim is almost certainly a statutory supervisor/manager excluded from NLRA protection, so *McLaren Macomb*, 372 NLRB No. 58 (2023), is unlikely to invalidate his covenant directly. The greater risks are (i) the clause has **no carve-outs** for SEC whistleblowing (Rule 21F-17), agency charges, truthful testimony or legally protected speech, (ii) the perpetual, “casts in an unfavorable light” standard and the Company’s weak, “instruct”-only reciprocal obligation, and (iii) reusing the same language in non-supervisory separation agreements. The separation agreement should include a standard protected-activity carve-out.")
B("**Unsigned copies.** The copies provided to us have blank signature lines. N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-4 requires a non-compete to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged. Please send fully executed copies of all three instruments (and the 2019 Omnibus Plan) before the Board relies on this analysis.")
B("**Recommended strategy:** treat the separation agreement as the cure. Offer new consideration (e.g., cash in lieu of, or acceleration of, the 7,000-RSU Tranche 3 worth ~$105,700 at $15.10, or other enhancement) in exchange for a re-executed, correctly numbered, narrowly tailored restrictive covenant package (role-based non-compete, customer and employee non-solicits, tolling, notice-to-new-employer, clarified clawback mechanics and protected-activity carve-outs).  ["Executive Employment Agreement (Original Agreement)", "Executed July 22, 2021; effective Aug. 15, 2021. N.C. law (§ 9.1); exclusive forum: state/federal courts in Mecklenburg County, N.C. P("**Items we need to finalize the analysis:** fully executed copies of all three instruments; the 2019 Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan (it controls over the RSU Agreement except Articles VI–VII and may contain its own forfeiture, clawback, Committee-discretion, governing-law or forum terms); the Company’s Dodd-Frank/Rule 10D-1 clawback policy; closing prices on March 1, 2023 and March 1, 2024 (and the settlement records showing shares withheld for taxes); Board/Compensation Committee minutes establishing any “minimum revenue targets” for 2023–2024; the FY2024 bonus determination and payment date; Manheim’s age (OWBPA); and the Lakeshore Asset Purchase Agreement (to confirm whether Manheim had any seller-side or Lakeshore-era covenants and the structure of the acquisition).")

H("III. Threshold Issue: The Amendment’s Cross-References Do Not Match the Original Agreement", 1)
P("Every operative section of the Amendment refers to a section number that either does not exist in the Original Agreement or refers to an unrelated provision. The table below maps each reference to the provision we believe was intended.")

 ["§ 6", "“Section 7(c)” Non-Solicitation of Employees", "Same (reserved Article VII)", "§ 8.3", "Two potentially coexisting employee non-solicits (18 vs. 12 months)."],
 ["§ 7", "New “Section 7(e)” Garden Leave", "Reserved Article VII", "New provision; references “Section 5(c)” (Cause) and “Section 5(d)” (severance) — actually §§ 1.3 and 6.2(b)", "Offset mechanics rest on non-existent cross-references."],
 ["§ 8", "“Section 5(c)” Cause, add clause (vi)", "§ 5 is Representations and Warranties; Cause is § 1.3", "§ 1.3", "Manheim can argue the revenue-target Cause prong never became part of § 1.3 (and thus of the RSU Agreement’s Cause definition)."],
 ["§ 9", "New “Section 7(f)” Forfeiture-for-Breach", "Reserved Article VII; covers covenants “set forth in this Section 7”", "Intended to cover all covenants (Article VIII)", "Literal text may not reach §§ 8.2, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, which remain in Article VIII."],
 ["§ 10", "New “Section 8(e)” DTSA Notice", "Article VIII has §§ 8.1–8.8 (no lettered subsections)", "Article VIII", "Notice still effective as an “update” under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b)(3)."],
], [0.65, 1.15, 1.6, 1.35, 1.95], size=8.5)
P("**Analysis.** A North Carolina court will try to give effect to the parties’ evident intent, and the Amendment’s substantive content (e.g., “Non-Competition,” “Non-Solicitation of Employees”) makes the intended targets reasonably clear. Pinnacle would argue scrivener’s error and, if necessary, reformation for mutual mistake (which requires clear, cogent and convincing evidence). But three features cut the other way: (1) Section 9.3 of the Original Agreement conditions any amendment on specific reference to the provision being amended; (2) Article VII was expressly reserved and “shall have no force or effect unless and until amended in accordance with Section 9.3,” which supports reading the Amendment as populating Article VII with **additional** covenants rather than replacing Article VIII; and (3) restrictive covenants are construed strictly against the drafter-employer. H("VIII. Enforceability Risks, Drafting Gaps and Ambiguities", 1)
H("A. Consideration for the First Amendment (Your First Concern)", 2)
P("North Carolina enforces a non-compete only if it is (1) in writing, (2) part of an employment contract, (3) based on valuable consideration, (4) reasonable as to time and territory, and (5) not against public policy. *United Laboratories, Inc. v. Kuykendall*, 322 N.C. 643 (1988); N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-4. When a covenant is signed at the start of employment, the employment itself is sufficient consideration. When a covenant is entered into — or materially expanded — after employment has begun, it must be supported by **new** consideration, such as a raise, a promotion, a bonus or other new benefit; continued at-will employment is not enough. *Kadis v. Britt*, 224 N.C. 154 (1944); *Young v. Mastrom, Inc.*, 99 N.C. App. 120 (1990); see also *Whittaker General Medical Corp. v. Daniel*, 324 N.C. 523 (1989).")
P("Here, the Amendment recites only “continued employment” and “the designation of Executive as Chief Revenue Officer.” Manheim has been CRO since August 15, 2021 (EA § 2.1), so the “designation” confers nothing new. His salary and target bonus stayed the same, and his maximum bonus fell from 200% to 150%. Pinnacle’s best arguments are (i) the removal of the 10% uniform salary-reduction carve-out (Amend. § 3), (ii) the shorter 12-month employee non-solicit, and (iii) the expanded responsibilities and enhanced profile from overseeing Lakeshore. None is likely to be persuasive: (i) and (ii) are marginal, and expanded duties are an additional burden on the employee, not a benefit to him. Generic “other good and valuable consideration” recitals do not cure the problem. **Risk: High** that the broadened non-compete (24 months; 10% threshold; home fragrance; Canada revenue), the no-hire/former-employee prongs of the employee non-solicit, and arguably Cause clause (vi), the 90-day notice and the forfeiture-for-breach terms are unenforceable for lack of consideration.")
P("**Fallback.** If the Amendment fails, Pinnacle should be able to rely on the Original Agreement’s covenants (supported by initial-hire consideration) and the RSU covenant (supported by the RSU grant). Manheim may argue the Amendment “amended and restated” — i.e., extinguished — the original non-compete, leaving no non-compete if the replacement is void; Pinnacle has the better of that argument (a failed amendment should not destroy the original bargain, and the Amendment’s numbering never actually referenced § 8.1), but the issue should be anticipated. **Planning assumption: an 18-month EA non-compete and a 12-month RSU non-compete.**")

H("B. Scope of the Non-Competes (Activity, Territory and Duration)", 2)
B("**“Any capacity” overbreadth.** Both EA versions prohibit employment by a qualifying Person in any capacity, and RSU § 6.2 bars working for a Competitive Business “in any other capacity.” North Carolina courts have repeatedly refused to enforce covenants that would bar an employee from working for a competitor in any role, including roles unrelated to what he did for the employer. *E.g.*, *Okuma America Corp. v. Bowers*, 181 N.C. App. 85 (2007); *VisionAIR, Inc. v. James*, 167 N.C. App. 504 (2004); *Hartman v. W.H. Odell & Assocs., Inc.*, 117 N.C. App. 307 (1994). Applied to multi-segment “big three” competitors, the clause would bar Manheim from, e.g., a non-sales role in an unrelated division. **Risk: Moderate–High.**")
B("**No judicial rewriting.** North Carolina follows a strict blue-pencil rule: a court may strike distinctly separable provisions but may not rewrite or narrow an overbroad covenant, and parties cannot contractually authorize a court to do so. *Whittaker*, 324 N.C. 523; *Beverage Systems of the Carolinas, LLC v. Associated Beverage Repair, LLC*, 368 N.C. 693 (2016). EA § 9.4 provides only for severance, and there is no reformation clause. An overbroad covenant therefore fails in its entirety.")
B("**Territory and duration.** U.S. and Canada is defensible for a CRO with national account responsibility, but time and territory are considered together, and North Carolina courts examine where the employee actually worked and had customer contact. 18 months is within the range North Carolina courts routinely enforce; 24 months nationwide-plus-Canada increases risk. **Risk: Moderate.** The entity-based revenue test (rather than a competing-products or competing-role test) also captures companies whose relevant business does not compete with Pinnacle’s premium segment.")
B("**Customer non-solicit** is the most defensible covenant (tied to accounts with Material Contact), although the combined 24-month lookback and 24-month restriction will be weighed together (cf. *Farr Associates, Inc. v. Baskin*, 138 N.C. App. 276 (2000)) and the “knowledge of” prospective-customer prong is broad. **Risk: Low–Moderate.**")
B("**FTC Non-Compete Rule.** The FTC rule was set aside nationwide in *Ryan LLC v. FTC* (N.D. Tex. Aug. 20, 2024), and in any event would have grandfathered existing non-competes with “senior executives” such as Manheim. It does not affect this analysis, though the new Administration’s position and any appeal should be monitored.")

H("C. Overlapping Covenants and Equity Interplay (Your Second Concern)", 2)
P("See Part V.B–C. In short: (1) the instruments do not supersede one another — RSU § 6.3 makes them cumulative and RSU § 8.3 confirms the EA is unmodified; (2) the RSU non-compete is the most defensible on consideration but is the shortest and is limited to household cleaning; (3) only the RSU non-compete triggers the equity clawback; (4) the differing “Restricted Period” definitions and competitor tests invite a construction-against-drafter argument that the shortest/narrowest version reflects the parties’ intent; and (5) the Delaware choice of law is likely to be tested in a North Carolina court. The inconsistency also undermines the reasonableness narrative: Pinnacle itself drafted a 12-month household-cleaning-only restriction in March 2022, which Manheim will cite as evidence that 24 months and a broader product scope were not necessary to protect Pinnacle’s interests.")

H("D. Non-Disparagement and Confidentiality — NLRB and Other Public-Policy Limits (Your Fourth Concern)", 2)
B("**McLaren Macomb, 372 NLRB No. 58 (Feb. 21, 2023)**, held that merely proffering a severance agreement with broad confidentiality and non-disparagement terms to an NLRA-covered “employee” violates Section 8(a)(1). The NLRA excludes supervisors (29 U.S.C. § 152(3), (11)) and managerial employees (*NLRB v. Bell Aerospace Co.*, 416 U.S. 267 (1974)), and the General Counsel’s implementing guidance (GC 23-05, Mar. 22, 2023) acknowledged that supervisors are generally not covered. As an officer reporting to the CEO with authority over the sales organization, Manheim is almost certainly excluded. **Direct risk as to Manheim: Low.** The doctrine’s status is also in flux with the change in Administration.")
B("**Residual NLRA risk:** (i) if the same non-disparagement language appears in agreements with non-supervisory sales staff (including Lakeshore employees), those provisions are exposed; (ii) a narrow exception exists where a supervisor is disciplined for refusing to commit an unfair labor practice or for testifying in Board proceedings; and (iii) any provision preventing Manheim from assisting employees in Board proceedings could be challenged.")
B("**SEC Rule 21F-17 (17 C.F.R. § 240.21F-17).** Pinnacle appears to be publicly traded (the RSU Agreement references a national securities exchange and Section 10D). The SEC has repeatedly brought settled enforcement actions against issuers whose confidentiality, non-disparagement and release terms lacked an express carve-out for communicating with the SEC. Neither EA § 8.4 nor § 8.5 contains one, and the DTSA notice expressly declines to modify them. **Risk: Moderate** — fix in the separation agreement and in future forms.")
B("**Speak Out Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 19401–19404).** A pre-dispute non-disparagement or non-disclosure clause such as § 8.5 is unenforceable with respect to sexual assault and sexual harassment disputes.")
B("**Drafting issues.** The “casts in an unfavorable light” standard is vague and extends to past and present employees, shareholders and products; it is perpetual; it contains no exception for truthful testimony, legal process or statements required by law (in tension with the cooperation duty in § 8.6); and the Company’s reciprocal obligation is merely to “instruct” current officers and directors (no liability for their statements, no coverage of future officers, no corporate statements). Courts are reluctant to enjoin speech, so the practical remedy is severance forfeiture, which itself depends on resolving the Amendment’s “Section 7” reference defect.")
B("**Separation agreement recommendation:** include an express protected-activity carve-out (SEC, EEOC, NLRB, OSHA and other agencies; truthful testimony; Speak Out Act; NLRA Section 7 rights to the extent applicable), a 409A-compliant structure, and, if Manheim is 40 or older, OWBPA-compliant 21/7-day periods.")

P("Clause (vi) requires failure “to achieve minimum revenue targets for two (2) consecutive fiscal quarters, as determined by the Board … in its reasonable discretion.” To rely on it, Pinnacle must show (i) the Amendment validly added clause (vi) to § 1.3 despite the “Section 5(c)” reference and the consideration issue, (ii) the Board actually established **minimum** revenue targets (as opposed to plan or stretch targets) with sufficient specificity and communicated them, (iii) two consecutive quarterly misses, and (iv) a reasonable Board determination. Given your concern about documentation, we agree that a without-Cause posture is prudent; a contested Cause termination would put the full severance and the RSU clawback in dispute and invite a breach-of-contract and wage claim.")

P("North Carolina enforces a non-compete only if it is (1) in writing, (2) part of an employment contract, (3) based on valuable consideration, (4) reasonable as to time and territory, and (5) not against public policy. *United Laboratories, Inc. v. Kuykendall*, 322 N.C. 643 (1988); N.C. Gen. Stat. § 75-4. When a covenant is signed at the start of employment, the employment itself is sufficient consideration. When a covenant is entered into — or materially expanded — after employment has begun, it must be supported by **new** consideration, such as a raise, a promotion, a bonus or other new benefit; continued at-will employment is not enough. *Kadis v. Britt*, 224 N.C. 154 (1944); *Young v. Mastrom, Inc.*, 99 N.C. App. 120 (1990); see also *Whittaker General Medical Corp. v. Daniel*, 324 N.C. 523 (1989).")
P("Here, the Amendment recites only “continued employment” and “the designation of Executive as Chief Revenue Officer.” Manheim has been CRO since August 15, 2021 (EA § 2.1), so the “designation” confers nothing new. His salary and target bonus stayed the same, and his maximum bonus fell from 200% to 150%. Pinnacle’s best arguments are (i) the removal of the 10% uniform salary-reduction carve-out (Amend. § 3), (ii) the shorter 12-month employee non-solicit, and (iii) the expanded responsibilities and enhanced profile from overseeing Lakeshore. None is likely to be persuasive: (i) and (ii) are marginal, and expanded duties are an additional burden on the employee, not a benefit to him. Generic “other good and valuable consideration” recitals do not cure the problem. **Risk: High** that the broadened non-compete (24 months; 10% threshold; home fragrance; Canada revenue), the no-hire/former-employee prongs of the employee non-solicit, and arguably Cause clause (vi), the 90-day notice and the forfeiture-for-breach terms are unenforceable for lack of consideration.")
P("**Fallback.** If the Amendment fails, Pinnacle should be able to rely on the Original Agreement’s covenants (supported by initial-hire consideration) and the RSU covenant (supported by the RSU grant). Manheim may argue the Amendment “amended and restated” — i.e., extinguished — the original non-compete, leaving no non-compete if the replacement is void; Pinnacle has the better of that argument (a failed amendment should not destroy the original bargain, and the Amendment’s numbering never actually referenced § 8.1), but the issue should be anticipated. **Planning assumption: an 18-month EA non-compete and a 12-month RSU non-compete.**")

H("B. Scope of the Non-Competes (Activity, Territory and Duration)", 2)
B("**“Any capacity” overbreadth.** Both EA versions prohibit employment by a qualifying Person in any capacity, and RSU § 6.2 bars working for a Competitive Business “in any other capacity.” North Carolina courts have repeatedly refused to enforce covenants that would bar an employee from working for a competitor in any role, including roles unrelated to what he did for the employer. *E.g.*, *Okuma America Corp. v. Bowers*, 181 N.C. App. 85 (2007); *VisionAIR, Inc. v. James*, 167 N.C. App. 504 (2004); *Hartman v. W.H. Odell & Assocs., Inc.*, 117 N.C. App. 307 (1994). Applied to multi-segment “big three” competitors, the clause would bar Manheim from, e.g., a non-sales role in an unrelated division. **Risk: Moderate–High.**")
B("**No judicial rewriting.** North Carolina follows a strict blue-pencil rule: a court may strike distinctly separable provisions but may not rewrite or narrow an overbroad covenant, and parties cannot contractually authorize a court to do so. *Whittaker*, 324 N.C. 523; *Beverage Systems of the Carolinas, LLC v. Associated Beverage Repair, LLC*, 368 N.C. 693 (2016). EA § 9.4 provides only for severance, and there is no reformation clause. An overbroad covenant therefore fails in its entirety.")
B("**Territory and duration.** U.S. and Canada is defensible for a CRO with national account responsibility, but time and territory are considered together, and North Carolina courts examine where the employee actually worked and had customer contact. 18 months is within the range North Carolina courts routinely enforce; 24 months nationwide-plus-Canada increases risk. **Risk: Moderate.** The entity-based revenue test (rather than a competing-products or competing-role test) also captures companies whose relevant business does not compete with Pinnacle’s premium segment.")
B("**Customer non-solicit** is the most defensible covenant (tied to accounts with Material Contact), although the combined 24-month lookback and 24-month restriction will be weighed together (cf. *Farr Associates, Inc. v. Baskin*, 138 N.C. App. 276 (2000)) and the “knowledge of” prospective-customer prong is broad. **Risk: Low–Moderate.**")
B("**FTC Non-Compete Rule.** The FTC rule was set aside nationwide in *Ryan LLC v. FTC* (N.D. Tex. Aug. 20, 2024), and in any event would have grandfathered existing non-competes with “senior executives” such as Manheim. It does not affect this analysis, though the new Administration’s position and any appeal should be monitored.")

Bell Aerospace Co.*, 416 U.S. 267 (1974)), and the General Counsel’s implementing guidance (GC 23-05, Mar. 22, 2023) acknowledged that supervisors are generally not covered. B("**Speak Out Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 19401–19404).** A pre-dispute non-disparagement or non-disclosure clause such as § 8.5 is unenforceable with respect to sexual assault and sexual harassment disputes.")
B("**Drafting issues.** The “casts in an unfavorable light” standard is vague and extends to past and present employees, shareholders and products; it is perpetual; it contains no exception for truthful testimony, legal process or statements required by law (in tension with the cooperation duty in § 8.6); and the Company’s reciprocal obligation is merely to “instruct” current officers and directors (no liability for their statements, no coverage of future officers, no corporate statements). B("**Separation agreement recommendation:** include an express protected-activity carve-out (SEC, EEOC, NLRB, OSHA and other agencies; truthful testimony; Speak Out Act; NLRA Section 7 rights to the extent applicable), a 409A-compliant structure, and, if Manheim is 40 or older, OWBPA-compliant 21/7-day periods.")

P("See Parts IV.G and VI.B. The offset is unavailable in a Company-initiated termination; where it does apply, it prevents double payment rather than creating savings.
